knowledgeAnswers.rationale: A correction keeps the original visible, moves the reading to the sheet for its own tank type, and records the reason. Averaging or deleting the entry destroys the record.
Equipment used for one tank can carry contamination or disease into another. Dedicated, cleaned equipment limits that risk.
An instrument that is not calibrated gives a result that is not valid. The instrument is calibrated and the reading is repeated, and the calibration status is recorded.

practicalCriteria: Learner calibrates a salinity instrument against the specified solution, and records the date and the result of the check
Learner corrects a misplaced entry on a training sheet with a single line, the correct value, initials, date and reason
Learner samples a training tank from the planned open-water point, not from the outlet or the heater area, and labels the sample before leaving the point
passRule: Knowledge checks: 80 per cent pass mark. With three questions, all three must be correct. Practical sign-off is assessed separately by observation and is not verified by this quiz.
evidenceRequired: Sample record for the training tank, with time, temperature, method and tester
Correction log entry for the training sheet
Assessor observation of the sampling point and labelling
stopWorkCriteria: A marine reading written on a freshwater sheet and not corrected
Use of a sampling container for two tanks without cleaning between them
Use of an instrument or reagent that is out of calibration or past expiry
